verses.text: Those of us who are strong ought to carry the weaknesses of those who aren't, instead of looking out only for ourselves.
Each of us should look out for our neighbor's good and build them up.
Even Christ didn't live to please himself. As Scripture says, ‘The insults aimed at you fell on me.’
Everything written long ago was written to teach us, so that through endurance and the encouragement of Scripture we could have hope.
May the God who gives endurance and encouragement help you live in harmony with one another, following Christ Jesus,
so that together, with one voice, you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So welcome one another, just as Christ welcomed you, to God's glory.
I mean that Christ became a servant to the circumcised to show God's truthfulness by confirming the promises made to the patriarchs,
and so that the Gentiles would glorify God for his mercy. As Scripture says, ‘I will praise you among the Gentiles and sing to your name.’
Again it says, ‘Rejoice, you Gentiles, with his people.’
And again, ‘Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles; let all peoples praise him.’
Isaiah also says, ‘The root of Jesse will come, one who rises to rule the nations; the Gentiles will put their hope in him.’
May the God of hope fill you with every kind of joy and peace as you trust him, so that by the Holy Spirit's power your hope will overflow.
My brothers and sisters, I'm convinced that you're full of goodness, filled with knowledge, and able to guide one another.
Still, I've written to you quite boldly in places to refresh your memory, because of the grace God gave me
to serve Christ Jesus among the Gentiles. I serve like a priest with God's Good News, so that the Gentiles may become an offering acceptable to God, made holy by the Holy Spirit.
So I have reason to take pride in my service to God through Christ Jesus.
I won't claim anything except what Christ has accomplished through me to bring the Gentiles to obey God, by what I've said and done,
through powerful signs and wonders, by the power of God's Spirit. From Jerusalem all the way to Illyricum, I've fully proclaimed the Good News about Christ.
My goal has been to share the Good News where Christ wasn't already known, so I wouldn't build on someone else's foundation.
As Scripture says, ‘Those who were never told about him will see, and those who haven't heard will understand.’
That's why I've been kept from coming to you so many times.
But now I have no more place to work in these regions, and for many years I've wanted to visit you.
I hope to see you when I travel to Spain and be helped on my way there by you—after I've enjoyed your company for a while.
But for now I'm going to Jerusalem to serve God's people there.
The believers in Macedonia and Achaia were glad to take up a contribution for the poor among God's people in Jerusalem.
They were glad to do it, and they do owe them something. Since the Gentiles shared in the Jews' spiritual blessings, they should serve them with material blessings too.
Once I've delivered this gift and made sure they receive it, I'll travel to Spain by way of your city.
I know that when I come to you, I'll come with the full blessing of Christ's Good News.
Brothers and sisters, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit's love, I urge you to join me in praying to God for me.
Pray that I'll be rescued from the disobedient in Judea and that my service in Jerusalem will be welcomed by God's people there.
Then, if God wills, I can come to you with joy and find rest with you.
May the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
